subject: Private VPC deployment: CI gating, telemetry, and safe-deploy checklist
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private VPC deployment: CI gating, telemetry, and safe-deploy checklist

Team —

I'm opening a short thread to consolidate decisions for AcmeCorp's upcoming private VPC rollout (gitlab MR linked below). Primary asks: tighten CI gating across terraform/helm/ansible, define telemetry signals for abort/fallback, and enumerate merge-blocker criteria so we can sign off before on-prem testing.

Quick context: Acme wants a dedicated VPC with cross-tenant routing disabled, encrypted tfstate in their S3-compatible store, and a brief on-prem smoke test window the week of 2027-05-17. We have a multi-repo change touching: 
- infra/terraform/enclave (tfstate, backends, locks)
- charts/privstack (helm values for multi-az, egress routing)
- ansible/playbooks/bootstrap (vault usage, secret propagation)

Proposed outputs from this thread:
- a short preflight CI job (preflight-job.yaml) that runs: terraform plan with remote backend validation, helm template + values lint, ansible --check for critical playbooks
- telemetry-matrix.csv with signals to track (failed plans, KV cache misses, helm template diffs, long-running ansible tasks)
- merge-blocker-checklist.pdf (attached) with gating criteria for automatic merges

Please review the attachments and call out any items that MUST be checked in CI. I want owners and ETA by EOD 2027-05-02 so we can land the MR and schedule their on-site tests.

Gitlab MR: https://gitlab.redwood.internal/privstack/mr/4281
Drive checklist: https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/priv-ci-telemetry-checklist

Thanks —
Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment: CI gating, telemetry, and safe-deploy checklist

Marcus — good framing. A few immediate notes after scanning the MR and attachments: 

1) Terraform state and locking
- We must enforce remote state encryption + state locking for the Acme S3-compatible bucket. Add a terraform plan check that verifies backend config (backend.hcl) is pointing to the encrypted path and that state locking is enabled (dynamodb style or advisory lock). If not, job should fail and list remediation steps.

2) Preflight job (preflight-job.yaml)
- Add a small smoke apply step for non-destructive resources (tagging, namespaces). This should run with a short timeout (10m) and clear logs sent to the CI artifact for audit.

3) Helm values and imagePullPolicy
- Helm templates must include strict imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent for airgapped clusters we need documented image staging flow. Add a helm-lint stage that runs kubeval against rendered templates for the target k8s version.

4) Secrets and Ansible
- Ansible vault passwords must not be in the repo. We need the CI job to validate that vault-encrypted files exist and that ansible-vault --diff returns no plaintext leaks. Include a link to the runbook: https://docs.redwood.internal/runbooks/priv-deploy-preflight (added to related links).

I'll attach a small preflight job snippet (preflight-job.yaml) that we can iterate on.

Irene
Engineering Manager, Platform

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment: CI gating, telemetry, and safe-deploy checklist

Adding network perspective — thanks Marcus/Irene. Two things we must not gloss over: 

- Egress SNI routing and TLS inspection: Acme's perimeter boxes do TLS inspection and SNI rewriting in some pockets. Helm charts must not rely on DNS-based egress rules that assume SNI passthrough. We should include a network-sim job that uses a small attacker-client container to exercise outbound flows and validate SNI/eTLD behavior.

- Backpressure/queueing for control-plane ops: when we run a canary or bootstrap we should cap concurrent job spawns (Helm hooks + Ansible forks) to avoid overloading their control-plane. For terraform, add a concurrency flag in the CI runner (TF_CONCURRENCY=2) and monitor apply durations in telemetry.

Also: suggest a small traffic-sim test with 500 synthetic inference requests over 10 minutes to observe KV cache warmups and egress rate-limits. I'll add expected thresholds to telemetry-matrix.csv.

Karthik
Staff Network Engineer
From: AcmeCorp Ops <ops@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment: CI gating, telemetry, and safe-deploy checklist

Marcus/Irene/Karthik —

Thanks for the detailed checklist. A couple notes from Acme infra: 

- Firewall rules: we can open only a narrow set of egress destinations during the on-site window. Attached is our allowlist (acme-fw-allowlist.txt). Please confirm which control-plane endpoints Redwood needs to reach (we will not open broad 0.0.0.0/0).

- Image staging for airgapped nodes: we will host a local registry; please provide an image staging script or documented steps for the imagePullPolicy flow.

- Testing window: 2027-05-17 09:00–17:00 local. Our network team will be on standby.

We can also provide a small set of sample credentials for the S3-compatible store for validation in your CI (short-lived).

—Sam (AcmeCorp)
Senior Platform Engineer
ops@acme.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: AcmeCorp Ops <ops@acme.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment: CI gating, telemetry, and safe-deploy checklist

Sam / Acme team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the allowlist. Action items captured below (owner / ETA):

- Marcus: update MR to include TF backend validation step and TF_CONCURRENCY default = 2 (ETA: 2027-05-02 EOD) — DONE (pushed new commit).
- Irene: add helm-lint + kubeval stage and include image staging doc pointer (ETA: 2027-05-04).
- Karthik: add network-sim job + traffic-sim harness and thresholds to telemetry-matrix.csv (ETA: 2027-05-04).
- Mina: add ansible-vault validation into preflight-job.yaml and ensure artifacts are archived for audit (ETA: 2027-05-04).

Sam: we'll send a short list of control-plane egress hosts that the CI runner needs open before the test window. Expect that list in the morning. We will also provide an image staging script for your local registry.

Decision summary: preflight CI will be mandatory for merging. Merge-blocker checklist will be enforced by the CI pipeline MR checks. If any preflight step fails, the MR cannot be merged and a human owner must acknowledge a manual override in the MR comments.

Attaching updated merge-blocker-checklist.pdf and telemetry-matrix.csv for versioned reference.

Marcus
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, AcmeCorp Ops <ops@acme.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment: CI gating, telemetry, and safe-deploy checklist

Thanks all — closing the loop from CI/ops side. Quick status: 

- I pushed a pipeline update that runs the preflight job in a protected stage. It validates backend.hcl, runs ansible --check against vaulted files, and renders helm templates with kubeval. Artifacts are stored for 30d. MR: https://gitlab.redwood.internal/privstack/mr/4281

- Added an explicit check to fail the merge if any terraform plan includes changes to VPC-level resources without a signed approval comment (a short MR label + comment flow).

- Telemetry hooks: exported two signals into prometheus (priv_preflight_failures_total, preflight_apply_duration_seconds) and wired them to the dashboard in the drive checklist. I added thresholds per Karthik's traffic-sim matrix.

If Acme can open the control-plane allowlist tomorrow we will run a dry-run and share results.

Mina
CI/CD Engineer
